eyebrow: Enterprise Security Architecture, GRC & Risk Management · Chapter 6
subtitle: Lesson 21 · Third-Party and Vendor Risk Management

eyebrow: The idea this whole chapter builds on

steps.label: The function moves to the vendor
steps.sub: Payroll, cloud hosting, facilities access, software you run in-house

steps.label: The accountability does not
steps.sub: A vendor's failure is still your incident, your exposure

steps.label: Regulators, customers, and your board agree
steps.sub: None of them treat "the vendor did it" as a closed case

eyebrow: The real pattern, not a hypothetical
code:
Stolen vendor credentials  -> retailer breach via an HVAC contractor's remote access
Poisoned software update   -> 2020 build-process compromise reached thousands of customers
Mass exploitation, 1 tool  -> 2023 file-transfer vulnerability hit hundreds of organizations

Common thread: the victims' OWN controls were not the weak point.
caption: Three different mechanisms, one lesson: the entry point was a vendor relationship each time.

eyebrow: It doesn't stop one hop away

steps.label: Your cloud provider's own subcontractors
steps.sub: Data center operations you never signed a contract with

steps.label: Your SaaS vendor's underlying cloud infrastructure
steps.sub: A layer you have no direct visibility into

steps.label: Ask who your vendor relies on
steps.sub: Not just what they do with your data

code:
GDPR:  data controller (you) decides why/how data is processed
       -> stays accountable even when a processor vendor handles it

HIPAA: covered entity (you) signs a Business Associate Agreement
       -> stays accountable to regulators for patient data either way
caption: A contract can allocate cost after a breach. It cannot make a regulator treat it as someone else's problem.

subtitle: Turning "we trust this vendor" into an actual, tiered assessment process.
